# Authorized player-only Jail continuation

Anya's latest instruction supersedes the Pokemon custody, storage, login-fence and callback-view investigations. Leave Pokemon to their own mod's ordinary behavior. Do not read, confiscate, restore, modify or intercept Pokemon from Jail behavior. Remove only Jail's nonempty-party admission check. Escaping the actual cell must kill the player character through the existing journal-bound death path and automatically invoke native player respawn inside the verified jail without a client click.

This work is isolated on codex/jail-player-only-autorespawn from shared head 5948ccabbfc24f81e620f7e3504e0906e4a50108. The shared branch and every earlier source/evidence file remain unchanged. Do not resume the older callback experiment or apply its reference candidate here. No production inclusion, release, installation or deployment is authorized.

Implementation is hosted-disposable test-mod-only around the unchanged reviewed pair. The admission replacement is generated from the exact current JailAdmissions boundary, deleting only the explicit nonempty-party loop. All inventory/accessory/origin/wallet and certificate checks remain. The server-side auto-respawn coordinator requires a verified HELD escape-death journal, authoritative dead player, matching stored inventory/origin receipts and a safe jail destination. It invokes the existing native respawn handler after five death ticks; it does not set a global gamerule or depend on a client Respawn request. Ambiguous deaths, canceled damage and unsafe destinations retain quarantine, rather than replaying death or duplicating items.

No old party test mod or Cobblemon mixin is loaded. Test fixture setup may create synthetic Pokemon solely to establish nonempty-party admission. It does not implement or certify Pokemon preservation. The other mod's ordinary death/save/login callbacks remain untouched.

Heavy builds and all game launches run only on GitHub-hosted disposable environments. No private saves are used. Human-origin and wallet support retain their prior bounded compatibility limits; this scope does not broaden those adapters.
